To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CRTC1-MAML2 fusion gene is required for the survival and growth of mucoepideoridm carcinoma cells in vitro and that these cells are sensitive to EGFR inhibitors.
CRTC1-MAML2-positive mucoepdermoid carcinoma cells require aberrantly activated Areg-Egfr signaling for cell growth and survival and are sensitive to Egfr inhibition.

CRTC1-MAML2 fusion-positive human mucoepidermal carcinoma cells require aberrantly activated AEGF-EGFR signaling for their growth and survival, and that EGFR signaling is a promising therapeutic target for patients with unresectable CTC1-MAML2-positive mucoepidermoid carcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of CRTC1-MAML2 in mucoepidermal carcinoma and the importance of EGFR-targeted therapy in the treatment of this disease.
the role of CRTC1-MAML2 fusion gene in the growth and survival in MEC cancer.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying MEC tumorigenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our study revealed that the CRTC1-MAML2 fusion oncogenes promote the growth and survival in human MEC cells through activating the transcriptional coactivator CREB to induce AREG expression that subsequently activates the EGFR signaling in a paracrine and autocrine manner.
CRTC1-MAML2-positive MUCOEPIDERMOID carcinoma cells are dependent on aberrantly activated Areg-Egfr signaling for growth and survival, and are highly sensitive to EGFr-targeted therapy.
CRTC1-MAML2 positive MECs are highly sensitive to EGFr-targeting therapies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CRTC1-MAML2-positive Mucin Epithelial Carcinoma (MEC) cells require aberrantly activated AEG-EGFR signaling for growth and survival, which suggests that EGFR-targeting therapy may be beneficial for patients with advanced, inoperable CRTC1-MAM2L-positive MEC.
the CRTC1-MAML2 fusion oncogenes are required for the growth of MEC cells and that the fusion protein upregulates the expression of the AREG gene by activating CREB.
the CRTC1-MAML2 oncoproteins are required for the growth, survival and drug resistance of MEC cells and AREG is a critical downstream target gene for the CRTC1 - MAML2 oncoprotiens.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the AREG–EGF receptor pathway is required for the survival of MEC cells harboring the CRTC1-MAML2 fusion oncogenes, and that EGFR-targeting therapies may benefit patients with advanced MEC harboring the CTRC1-MAML2 translocation.
CRTC1-MAML2-positive MUCOEPIDERMAL CARCINOMA cells are highly sensitive to EGFr signaling inhibitors.
the AREG–EGRF axis is a critical driver of the CRTC-MAML2 fusion-positive MEC cells and is a potential therapeutic target for this disease.
